page: Microsoft Azure E16ps_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor featuring 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The CPU architecture is arm64, with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E16ps_v6 demonstrates strong memory performance. Its Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier, supported by strong large-block read-only memory bandwidth of 308.13 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 124.58 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 33.21 GB/sec. Conversely, CPU-bound workloads, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, fall into the average category. Large language model inference shows a tradeoff, with prompt processing on a medium 7B model registering as weak, while text generation remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture of the E16ps_v6 offers a high-density memory profile without the premium cost typically associated with x86 memory-optimized instances. However, users must account for tradeoffs, including the complete absence of local storage and the lack of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local disk space, such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, data buffering, and general-purpose ARM-compatible application serving.
